title: How to Write a Freelance Brief (With a Copyable Template)
h1: How to write a freelance brief that gets good work
description: What to include in a brief for a freelancer: goal, audience, deliverables, style, files and deadline, plus a simple template you can copy for any project.
intro: A brief is the document that tells a freelancer what you need. It does not need to be long or formal, but it does need to be clear. Most disappointing results are not caused by bad freelancers; they are caused by briefs that leave the important decisions to guesswork. This article explains what every brief should cover and gives you a simple template that works for design, writing, video, development and most other services.

faq.q: How long should a brief be?
faq.a: Usually one page is enough. Clarity matters more than length.

faq.q: What if I do not know what style I want?
faq.a: Collect a few examples you like and a few you dislike. Freelancers can read a lot from those.

faq.q: Should I send the brief before ordering?
faq.a: For bigger projects, send a short version first to confirm the seller can do it, then the full brief after ordering.

faq.q: Can I change the brief after the work starts?
faq.a: Small clarifications are normal. Big changes usually count as a new request and may cost extra.
Many will. Ask before sharing sensitive material, and share only what the job needs.
